title: MathTutorBench: Hard Scaffolding
summary: Three open-weight models write the next tutor turn in a math dialog; an LLM judge scores each turn against the real human teacher's response.

dataset.name: MathTutorBench (hard scaffolding subset)
dataset.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (treated as the more restrictive of two conflicting license statements in the source repo)

task_description: Each item is a math problem plus a partial student/teacher dialog. The model under test writes the next teacher turn (max 2 sentences) without giving away the answer.

metric.name: Judge score
metric.description: 0–1 score from an LLM judge (Qwen3.8-Max) comparing the model's turn to the real human teacher's turn; 0.50 means judged equal to the human.

notes: Judge, judge prompt, and reasoning-effort settings differ from Braintrust's original eval (not public), so exact score values are not expected to match — rank order and CI overlap are what's comparable.
Judge is Qwen3.8-Max, deliberately not one of the three models under test, to reduce self-preference and shared-lineage bias.
Results shown are the reasoning_effort=none condition; see the experiment README for the full run design.
